acceptance: SQL SSB runs at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 check every query's row count against benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py, through the shared expected-results registry or an equivalent single source, so the SQL and DataFrame paths cannot diverge
A wrong SSB query row count on a SQL platform fails the query and the run; an SSB scale factor with no recorded counts does not report passed on query evidence
Local DuckDB, DataFusion and SQLite SSB runs at SF 0.01 and 0.1 still report passed, with row_count_validation PASSED on every measured query
Tests fail without the change: a SQL SSB pass, a wrong count, and an unrecorded scale factor
The PR states how the change affects existing corpus SSB SQL bundles and cloud SSB results
context: Implemented in PR #3121 (branch fix/ssb-sql-row-count-validation, commit e9fab87d): SSB expected-results provider registered; SQL QueryValidator now checks SSB counts (wrong count fails, unrecorded scale SKIPs); new test file tests/unit/core/expected_results/test_ssb_sql_validation.py (9 tests); oracle coverage map regenerated. PR armed 2026-10-18; after merge, take and finish.
description:
SQL SSB runs report summary.validation "passed" even though no query result is checked. No SSB expected-results provider is registered. benchbox/core/expected_results/registry.py:229 register_benchmark_provider is called only for tpch (tpch_results.py:95) and tpcds (tpcds_results.py:117). QueryValidator therefore returns SKIP for every SSB query. The "passed" comes only from the load-time table row-count ranges in SSBRowCountStrategy (benchbox/platforms/base/validation.py:186, selected at :267). A SQL engine that returns wrong SSB query results would still be labelled passed and ranked as clean by results-data/validate_corpus.py.

PR #3065 (commit 87adc2cd9) added exact SSB per-query row counts at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 in benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py. Only the DataFrame path uses them (benchbox/core/dataframe/query_validation.py). They were deliberately left unregistered, because registering them changes SQL validation on every platform.

How found: during the #3065 work. A local `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark ssb --scale 0.1` on develop gives summary.validation "passed" and phases.validation PASSED, but all 39 measured query rows have no row_count_validation. The corpus SSB SQL bundles (results-data/bundles/ssb_*_sql_*.json) are the same.

Related: TPC-H SQL runs below SF 1 show the same pattern (passed with no query-level check). That case belongs to subscale-tpc-ranking-policy-20261016 and is not in scope here.
